title: Grok consumer overview
supports: Current consumer surfaces, core capabilities, platform availability
boundary: A current vendor capability description, not an independent measure of quality or effectiveness.

title: Grok product page
supports: Chat, Search, voice, Imagine, files and current consumer positioning
boundary: Marketing copy establishes advertised capability, not accuracy, learning impact or productivity gain.

title: Current Grok plans and pricing
supports: Dated plan table listing Grok 4.6 as a SuperGrok benefit and plan-dependent access
boundary: A plan benefit does not establish which ordinary chat mode routes to a model, and plans, prices and limits can change.

title: Grok FAQ: files, usage and product limits
supports: File types, approximate limits, platform differences, usage pool, retirement of Grok Studio
boundary: Limits and supported formats can change; the lesson asks learners to check the current interface before a consequential workflow.

title: Consumer privacy FAQ
supports: Training controls, Private Chat and deletion timing
boundary: This is a plain-language summary; the governing policies and local law control.

title: xAI security FAQ: data and privacy
supports: Surface-specific API, Grok Build terminal and consumer Build mode retention and training controls
boundary: Data handling differs across the API, terminal and consumer Build mode; each statement must remain attached to the exact surface and current settings.

title: Grok Build privacy and data lifecycle
supports: Inference transmission, local session history, team-level ZDR and Grok Build retention controls
boundary: ZDR is a team-level configuration, not a default; local history and xAI-side retention are separate data surfaces.

title: xAI privacy policy
supports: Consumer data processing and privacy rights
boundary: Privacy obligations vary by jurisdiction and account type; this course does not provide legal advice.

title: xAI consumer terms of service
supports: User responsibility for inputs, outputs and agentic actions
boundary: Terms can change and should be re-read before organisational or regulated use.

title: xAI acceptable use policy
supports: Safety boundaries for consequential and educational uses
boundary: The policy is a minimum platform boundary, not a substitute for professional, school or institutional safeguards.

title: xAI brand guidelines
supports: Accurate referential use, non-endorsement and attribution for generated material
boundary: The guidelines do not grant a blanket licence for every product screenshot or hosted media asset.

title: About Grok on X
supports: Separate X surface, controls and governing policies
boundary: The X experience has different settings and terms from grok.com; one opt-out does not imply the other is configured.

title: Grok 4.5 everywhere
supports: Latest explicit model statement for consumer Grok across web, X, iOS and Android
boundary: A dated release statement; model routing and labels can change after verification.

title: Grok 4.6
supports: Grok 4.6 availability in Grok Build, Cursor, API and partners
boundary: This page does not establish Grok 4.6 as the default ordinary consumer-chat model.

title: Grok 4: native tool use and search
supports: Historical explanation of web search, X search and tool traces
boundary: A 2025 workflow example, not a promise that the 2026 interface or entitlements are identical.

title: Grok Build on web and mobile
supports: Build access on every plan, preview, publish audience controls and GitHub export
boundary: Access remains subject to usage limits; the selected publish audience can be just you, anyone with the link or the whole internet, and generated software still requires security, accessibility and behaviour review.

title: Introducing consumer Build Mode
supports: Web and mobile Build preview, link publishing and the distinction from the terminal agent
boundary: Its early-beta plan and public-link wording were superseded by later access and audience-control guidance; this course uses it only for the preview and link-publishing workflow.

title: Introducing Grok Build
supports: Terminal installation, repository-aware planning, diff review, subagents, headless mode and ACP
boundary: This terminal coding-agent announcement is separate from consumer web and mobile Build mode, and dated access statements can change.

title: Grok Bot FAQ
supports: Current beta platforms and eligible plan families
boundary: Bot is a beta, plan-gated advanced surface; it is mapped but not required for this consumer course.

title: Skills in Grok
supports: Built-in Word, presentation, spreadsheet, PDF and Skill Creator workflows
boundary: Availability does not guarantee correct calculations, citations, formatting or organisational compliance.

title: Grok connector catalogue
supports: Available connectors, account provisioning and OAuth-based access
boundary: Connector permissions differ; the course requires learners to inspect the live scope screen and begin read-only.

title: Automations in Grok
supports: Scheduled and email-triggered runs, Run now, history, pause and edit controls
boundary: Scheduled availability and trigger entitlements can change; each run still requires outcome review.

title: Google Drive connector
supports: Google Drive OAuth scopes, real-time access, retention statement, training statement and revocation
boundary: These privacy and retention statements are specific to the Google Drive connector and must not be generalised to every connector.

title: Grok Imagine Image 2.0
supports: Image generation, quality mode, editing, references and resize tools
boundary: Generated media must be reviewed for rights, identity, accuracy, accessibility and preserved provenance.

title: Grok Imagine Video 1.5 with references
supports: Text, image, character and voice reference workflows
boundary: Reference controls began as a tiered rollout; learners must use only references they may lawfully and ethically use.

title: Introducing the Grok Excel add-in
supports: Selected-range analysis, formulas, charts and scenario questions in Excel
boundary: An official demonstration is not an independent validation of spreadsheet correctness or time savings; its visible returns claim requires a denominator the panel does not define.

title: Grok in Google Workspace
supports: Google Workspace add-on in Sheets, Slides and Docs with in-place editable changes
boundary: An advertised integration does not establish correctness or productivity outcomes, and availability can vary by account or domain.

title: xai-org/grok-build
supports: Interactive terminal agent, headless mode, repository inspection, edits and commands
boundary: Source code and README establish an implementable workflow, not coding quality or safety outcomes.

title: xai-org/grok-build-plugin-cc
supports: Read-only second-review and critique pattern
boundary: A supported review path does not prove every defect will be found; the human must inspect the diff and tests.

title: xai-org/xai-sdk-python
supports: Examples for search tools, citations, collections and file analysis
boundary: API examples do not imply an identical consumer UI or entitlement and do not validate answer correctness.

title: xai-org/xai-cookbook
supports: Structured-output and synthetic-persona writing workflow
boundary: An official showcase with synthetic data, not evidence of campaign, writing or productivity outcomes.

title: xai-org/grok-prompts
supports: Historical official templates that separate context, evidence, uncertainty and source quality
boundary: Published prompt templates do not prove current production prompting or reliable compliance.

title: Vectara hallucination leaderboard
supports: Bounded evidence that source-grounded summaries can still contain unsupported content
boundary: One benchmark setting with older Grok snapshots, a private corpus and a proprietary judge; no rate is generalised to current Grok.

title: InternScience/SGI-Bench
supports: Reproducible multi-stage scientific workflow benchmark containing a dated Grok-4 result
boundary: A version-specific benchmark is not evidence of laboratory validity, current-model performance or researcher productivity.

title: THU-MAIC/OpenMAIC
supports: A substantial implementation that supports Grok as one provider in lesson-prototyping workflows
boundary: Provider support is not evidence Grok improves learning or powered every demo; educators retain instructional responsibility.

title: n8n xAI integration documentation
supports: Third-party API credential and integration surface used to teach layer-by-layer troubleshooting
boundary: Third-party integration documentation establishes an API credential path, not end-to-end reliability or Grok model quality.
